Paragraph:
Translation: If I should cease to work, then all these worlds would be put to ruination. I would also be the cause of creating unwanted population, and I would thereby destroy the peace of all sentient beings.

Purport (Excerpt): Varna-sankara is unwanted population which disturbs the peace of the general society... We should... note carefully that although we have to follow in the footsteps of the Lord, we still have to remember that we cannot imitate Him... Following and imitating are not on the same level...
Situation/Problem_Faced: The destructive fallout of abandoning prescribed work, leading to social decay, disorder, and loss of peace.
Key_Teaching/Action_Taken: Krishna states that divine inaction would ruin the worlds and create chaotic social conditions (varna-sankara). He distinguishes between 'following' instructions vs. blindly 'imitating' powerful figures.
Outcome/Resolution: Arjuna understands that upholding his role is vital for preserving social harmony and preventing public collapse.

Mental_Health_Theme_Synonyms.Social Stability: Maintaining structure and order to protect collective mental peace
Mental_Health_Theme_Synonyms.Following vs. Imitating: Discerning between following wise guidance vs. irresponsibly mimicking actions beyond one's capacity
Mental_Health_Theme_Synonyms.Constructive Order: Upholding personal duties to prevent societal chaos

Spiritual_Psychological_Concept_Indian.Concept: Utseyur ime loka (Destruction/ruination of worlds caused by non-performance of duty)
Varna-sankara (Social chaos and unwanted population resulting from disruption of order)

Brief_Summary_Spiritual: Cessation of duty by the Lord or leaders would ruin societal structure, resulting in varna-sankara (social chaos) and destroying peace. Krishna also warns against foolishly imitating God's extraordinary acts instead of following His moral teachings.
Brief_Summary_Psychological: Maintaining structure and personal duty prevents life from collapsing into chaos. There is a key psychological distinction between following a mentor's principles and recklessly trying to copy their unique capabilities beyond your current capacity.
